coverage.boundaries: All actual range minima/maxima and select first/last options via scripts/check_course_inspectors.cjs; default demos inspect every frame against frozen traces and prefix-only steps.

scope: Reward-by-reward discount powers and finite sample return; immediate and discounted future portions.
Bellman success/terminal and failure/self-loop weighted contributions, one expectation backup, analytic fixed point, and the actual residual field meaning.
Every real synchronous value-iteration history sweep expanded into both state cells, followed by actual action-value comparison and explicit exit-on-tie policy.
TD single-transition target, true-terminal mask, signed error, and learning-rate update.
Same behavior sample under Q-learning max bootstrap versus SARSA recorded-action bootstrap.
Each epsilon-greedy action probability, each CDF boundary, fixed draw selection, and total probability.
Per-feature dot products, per-weight frozen-target half-gradients and updates, new prediction, and a labeled derived shared-feature probe.
Binary policy probabilities, sampled-action log score, advantage-weighted sample gradient, ascent update, and normalized new probability.

checks: All current demos, every real frame, stable unique cells, frozen trace immutability, no result/scene or future-frame access.
Each experiment changes actual parameters, verifies concrete before/after values, and rejects a damaged claimed output.
Independent discounted-return and Bellman expectation arithmetic, including the residual interpretation.
Independent synchronous history and one-sweep action-evaluation distinction; greedy tie handling.
True-terminal TD target and same-sample SARSA/Q-learning difference.
Exploration mass, fixed draws, and equality at a CDF boundary.
Half-gradient updates, shared-state probe, and overshoot with a larger learning rate.
Policy score checked against independent finite differences of log probability.

limits: Original finite arithmetic examples from the current catalog; no claim of full official CS234 lecture coverage or real policy training.
Each source model has four real computation frames. The planning loop is expanded within its actual history-producing frame; no synthetic timeline is added.
Bellman uses exact model-branch expectation; trajectory return, TD/Q update, fixed exploration draw, and policy-gradient item retain their sample meanings.
The approximation shared-feature probe is derived from already-computed weights and explicitly labeled; it is neither an extra training sample nor an asserted correct target.
Formula text uses four decimal places; numeric cells and experiment verification preserve full precision. The shared renderer controls value display.
Only the course-owned provider, tests, and this manifest are authored; no catalog, shared model, UI, build, browser, learning record, receipt, completion, or minute changes.
